chapter: Arranging for other bandleaders and closing talk
title: Why Fletcher rarely went out to hear bands
summary: Horace scouted clubs and told Fletcher about players to hire, while Fletcher stayed home writing for Goodman around the clock.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: And Fletcher didn't -- getting back to your question again, I'll elaborate a little more I didn't want to -- he didn't go around much, you know. Now like I used to frequent a lot of clubs where bands were playing because I used to just like jazz and would like the different bands and like the different soloists that came up in those days. In fact, I used to tell Fletcher, I said, "Smack, I went to a certain club last night and heard this band. Man, you ought to hear this trumpet player." This is how Fletcher sometimes would get some great musicians, you know, if the bands would break up, and I'd get the names, you know, and the telephone numbers, and I said, "You want to hear a guy play, man, this can can play," you know.

So he was never one for going out much. He stayed home. He was a good man at home. And he was busy writing, because when he was writing for Benny, that meant from 5:00 o'clock in the morning until 5:00 that afternoon and right on around, because Benny wouldn't mind calling you up anytime, you know. So it took it's physical toll on him, you know, so I think this is one of the reasons why he didn't get a chance to, you know, frequent the places like I did.
